Read the natality public-use file

Source: R/read.R
read_natality.Rd

Reads fields by byte position with vroom::vroom_fwf(), or, if a sharded Parquet directory (as written by natality_pack()) is available, queries that instead via DuckDB — same result, far less I/O. Bytes beyond the last documented field are never read, so a file whose records are longer than the guide says is read correctly as long as the documented fields are where the guide puts them (see diagnose_layout()).

Usage

read_natality(
  file = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  n_max = Inf,
  raw = FALSE,
  na_unknown = TRUE,
  year = 2025,
  parquet_dir = NULL,
  ...
)

Source

The fixed-width file itself is downloaded from NCHS at https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data_access/vitalstatsonline.htm#Downloadable; this function reads a copy already on disk and does not download it.

Arguments

file

Path to the fixed-width natality file. NULL (the default) resolves from NCHS_NAT_PATH or NCHS_NAT_PARQUET; see above.

cols

Field names to read. The default is every field except FILLER.

n_max

Number of records to read.

raw

If TRUE, return every field as the character code in the file.

na_unknown

For numeric fields, turn the documented "unknown", "not stated" and "not applicable" codes (e.g. DBWT 9999, BMI 99.9, ILLB_R 888/999, APGAR10 88) into NA.

year

Data year; see natality_years().

parquet_dir

A directory written by natality_pack() to query instead of file. NULL (the default) resolves from NCHS_NAT_PARQUET; see above. Ignored if file is given explicitly.

...

Passed to vroom::vroom_fwf() when reading text, e.g. num_threads. Ignored when reading from Parquet.

Value

A data.table. Numeric fields (kind == "numeric" in natality_layout()) are integer (BMI is double). Categorical fields are character codes, for use with label_natality(). Blank fields, which the guide uses for items not on the certificate or from non-reporting areas, are NA.

Choosing text vs Parquet

file and parquet_dir default to NULL, meaning "resolve from the environment": NCHS_NAT_PARQUET, if it names a directory with a storage.csv and at least one *.parquet file in it, is used; otherwise NCHS_NAT_PATH is used. Passing file or parquet_dir explicitly pins the source and skips that resolution. Either way the result has the same shape: same columns, same types, same na_unknown sentinel handling — see inst/adrs/ for the reasoning. Row order is not part of that contract: natality_pack() sorts and shards rows for compression (see its documentation), so reading from Parquet returns the same rows as from text, as a set, but not necessarily in the same order.

Examples

if (nchar(f <- Sys.getenv("NCHS_NAT_PATH"))>0) {
  z <- read_natality(f, n_max = 10000)
  z <- read_natality(f, cols = c("MAGER", "DBWT", "COMBGEST", "SEX"))
  } else { "NCHS_NAT_PATH not set in visible environment" }
#> [1] "NCHS_NAT_PATH not set in visible environment"
